heading: INT. HIGH COURT OF APPEAL - TIMBERED CHAMBER - MORNING

units.text: INT. HIGH COURT OF APPEAL - TIMBERED CHAMBER - MORNING
A hall of dark oak, high galleries, a vaulted ceiling hung with brass lamps that cast small circles of gold onto the polished floor.
Dust drifts through the light like slow snow.
At the far end, a raised bench carved with lions and vines.
JUDGE OYELARAN, 60s, in black robes and a silver wig, sits motionless.
Her pen hovers above a ledger.
In front of her, at the long mahogany table, sits SAMUEL BECKETT-LOWE, 50s, defense counsel, in a rumpled gown, thumbing a sheaf of notes he has already memorized.
Beside him, HANA KOBAYASHI, 30s, the junior, knees pressed together, a legal pad shaking slightly on her lap.
At the lectern stands ABDI WARSAME, 40s, the witness, in a suit that is too thin for the weather, hands folded so tightly the knuckles show.
Near the window, CLERK DOMINGO, 20s, thin, with a stack of exhibits cradled in his arms, shifts from foot to foot.
In the jury box, a woman in the front row, PETRA HOLLOWAY, 50s, juror seven, picks at a loose thread in her sleeve, her gaze fixed on Abdi's face.
Mr. Warsame, in your statement you said you were on the ferry at ten past six.
units.name: LOWE

units.text: Yes, sir.
units.name: WARSAME

units.text: And the ferry is eleven miles from the warehouse.
units.name: LOWE

units.text: About that.
units.name: WARSAME

units.text: Eleven miles. Twenty minutes by motorcar. Which means you could not have been at the warehouse at six-fifteen.
units.name: LOWE

units.text: No, sir.
units.name: WARSAME

units.text: Yet the prosecution's witness places you there.
units.name: LOWE

units.text: She is mistaken.
units.name: WARSAME

units.text: Or lying.
units.name: LOWE

units.text: Mr. Beckett-Lowe.
units.name: OYELARAN

units.text: Mistaken. Forgive me, Your Honor.
units.name: LOWE

units.text: Hana scribbles something.
Passes it to Lowe without looking at him.

He reads it, folds it into his sleeve, and lifts his chin toward the clerk, who steps forward with a bound folder, sets it before the witness, and retreats, while in the jury box Petra Holloway leans a fraction closer, and the judge turns a page, and the wind rattles the tall windows, and for a moment the whole chamber seems to hold itself as still as a held breath.
Exhibit twenty-two. A ticket stub.
units.name: LOWE

units.text: Yes.
units.name: WARSAME

units.text: Read the time.
units.name: LOWE

units.text: Six-oh-eight.
units.name: WARSAME

units.text: Thank you. And the location?
units.name: LOWE

units.text: The Eastside pier.
units.name: WARSAME

units.text: Eastside. Not the warehouse district.
units.name: LOWE

units.text: No, sir.
units.name: WARSAME

units.text: He glances at the jury, then at the floor.
Petra Holloway straightens in her seat.
No further questions.
units.name: LOWE

units.text: The Crown may cross-examine.
units.name: OYELARAN

units.text: A rustle through the gallery.
Nobody rises.
Hearing none, the witness is excused.
units.name: OYELARAN

units.text: Warsame steps down.
The Clerk gathers the folder.
Hana lets out a breath she has been holding for an hour.
Lowe finally smiles, thinly, and pats her arm without looking.
Petra Holloway folds the loose thread into her palm, closes her fist around it, and lets it go.
